draft.title: Nationalism
card: Nationalism is the belief that people who share a language, history and culture should rule themselves as a nation. It gives people a sense of belonging to a larger group.
In the 1800s nationalism helped to unite people who lived in many small states. Germany and Italy each became a single country this way.
Nationalism can also fuel rivalry. When nations are proud of their own strength and want more power, they may see other nations as threats.
This pride and rivalry between nations was one cause of the tensions that led to war in Europe in 1914.
draft.remember: Nationalism ties people to their nation, and it can unite a people or fuel rivalry.

a.q: Which belief is an example of nationalism?
opts: A people with one culture should rule themselves
A strong country should take over weaker lands
A people should be free to move wherever they like
A ruler should share power with an elected body
a.why: Nationalism is the belief that a people with a shared language, history and culture should rule themselves as a nation. Taking over other lands is imperialism, which is a different idea.
a.clue: Look for the belief about a shared identity and self-rule.

b.q: In the 1800s, many small states with a shared language became one Italy. Which idea best explains why many people supported this?
opts: They saw themselves as one nation and wanted self-rule
They wanted their rulers to take over lands overseas
They hoped to avoid rivalry with other European nations
They were made to move to Italy by other great powers
b.why: Many people saw themselves as one nation because they shared a language, history and culture, and they wanted to rule themselves. Taking over lands overseas is imperialism, and nationalism often added to rivalry rather than avoiding it.
b.clue: Think about what a shared language and history can lead people to want.

a.best: A people with one culture should rule themselves

b.best: They saw themselves as one nation and wanted self-rule

problems.detail: Why (a) defines imperialism ('Taking over other lands is imperialism'), a term that belongs to point 1. It should only be mentioned, not explained, here. Why (b) repeats this.
